A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FIRE research and provide readable text, equations, figures, tables and Appendices A–E. The appendices match after accounting for changed headers and pagination.

before.justification: v1 reports original visual-learning, language-model pretraining and reinforcement-learning experiments, plus ablations and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, ablations and computational measurements in Section 4 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: The constrained SFE/DfI objective, Newton–Schulz procedure, Algorithm 1 and layer-specific implementation in Appendix C are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet, WikiText-103/OpenWebText, Atari and HumanoidBench coverage. The warm-start, continual and class-incremental scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments. Figures 2–4 and Appendix D retain the same visual-learning baselines, LLM base/full-reset/S&P comparisons and RL comparisons including Plasticity Injection.

E3.justification: The data schedules, architectures, checkpoint choices, reset timing and evaluation metrics remain identical. Appendix E retains the same training budgets, optimizer settings and hyperparameter searches.

E4.justification: Section 4.4 and Appendix B retain the same iteration-count sensitivity, SFE/DfI/Hessian comparisons, computational-efficiency measurements, Newton–Schulz coefficient comparison and training-accuracy analyses.

E5.justification: Both report three seeds for vision and LLM experiments, five for reinforcement learning and ten trials for timing measurements. The plotted uncertainty displays and statistical reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–8 retain identical plotted results, and Table 1 retains the same timing and memory values. No numerical results, rankings or qualitative findings are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: The definitions, assumptions, Theorems 1–4 and constrained-optimization derivation are unchanged. Appendix A preserves the same lemmas, corollaries and proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about principled stability–plasticity balancing, efficient reinitialization and effectiveness across vision, language and reinforcement learning.

C2.justification: The explanations of convergence, stability and plasticity remain unchanged. Both retain the limitations concerning access to past data, small language models and untested continual fine-tuning.

D1.justification: The abstract newly advertises videos alongside code at the existing project page. This adds a small resource-access disclosure; the URL, implementation details, hardware information and hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference entries and research positioning are unchanged. Several introduction citations become parenthetical, without adding or removing sources.

P1.justification: v3 adds a Holiday Robotics affiliation, replaces the preprint header with an ICLR 2026 publication header, adjusts citation punctuation and expands the project-page sentence. The narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The added affiliation and text reflow alter front-page spacing and subsequent page breaks, moving the references and appendices. Figures 1–8 and Tables 1–10 retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the same method, theoretical support, experiments, results and limitations, including the appendices. The affiliation, formatting and resource-description edits provide minor editorial updates without meaningfully changing the paper’s overall clarity, rigor or reproducibility.
